answer: Sybil resistance arises when each challenge cryptographically binds a committed task instance to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse. The pulse supplies unpredictable, publicly verifiable entropy, while commit-reveal prevents participants from selecting favorable values. Consequently, automated swarms cannot precompute valid answers, reuse work, or farm challenges offline; each identity must perform fresh, timely work. “falcon,” “anchor,” and “ferrous” may serve as domain-separated labels, but provide no predictive advantage.
